metadata.title: AI Sovereignty Lab v0.4 Source Audit, Batch 3
scope: Israel AI data-center planning and grid constraints

audits.publisher: Tower Semiconductor / U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
audits.title: Tower Semiconductor Form 20-F for fiscal year 2025
exact_supported_claims: Tower Semiconductor Ltd. is incorporated in Israel and lists its principal executive offices in Migdal HaEmek, Israel.
Tower ceased Fab 1 production operations during 2025 and consolidated selected production flows into Fab 2 in Migdal HaEmek.
Fab 2 remains operational in Migdal HaEmek and supports specialty semiconductor processes ranging from 0.35 to 0.13 micron.
Fab 2 capabilities include analog, RF, power, mixed-signal, CMOS image-sensor and related specialty process technologies.
Tower operates a wider international manufacturing network through subsidiaries and partnerships outside Israel.
limitations: Tower's Israeli fab is a meaningful domestic fabrication capability, but it is not a leading-edge logic fab for frontier AI accelerators.
The filing does not support presenting Israel as domestically self-sufficient in EUV, HBM, advanced packaging or leading-edge accelerator fabrication.
The discontinued Fab 1 must not remain represented as an operational production fab.
audits.required_dataset_action: Add a Tower Semiconductor node in the Israel fabrication layer. Mark Fab 2 operational, Fab 1 production discontinued, and explicitly classify the capability as specialty semiconductor fabrication rather than leading-edge AI-chip manufacturing.

audits.title: Committee approval of the bill promoting AI server farms as national infrastructure
exact_supported_claims: The committee approved the Planning and Building Bill Amendment 168 for second and third readings.
The proposed definition covers an AI server farm whose electricity consumption for processing power is at least 50 MW.
The framework allows no more than ten plans per calendar year and no more than five plans in the Tel Aviv and Central districts combined.
Government authorization of a national-infrastructure plan is expected to consider contribution to Israeli AI use, electricity-system needs, energy efficiency and renewable energy.
limitations: The source describes the bill as approved by committee and must not be represented as a final operational data-center capacity figure.
A planning pathway does not establish that grid connection, generation, cooling or accelerator supply is available.
audits.required_dataset_action: Add a planning-and-regulation node for large AI data centers. Use 50 MW only as the legislative definition threshold, not as the capacity of an existing facility.

audits.title: AI and advanced technologies subcommittee discussion on data-center electricity demand
exact_supported_claims: The hearing summary attributes to the Electricity Authority an estimate that data centers represented approximately 0.5 percent of Israeli electricity consumption in 2024 and could represent approximately 5 to 7 percent in 2030.
The hearing summary reports approximately 300 MVA of connected data-center capacity in 2024 and approximately 2,500 MVA of requested connections through 2030.
Approximately 40 percent of connection requests were reported as concentrated in the Central district and Greater Tel Aviv.
The Electricity Authority was reported as stating that the average construction time for a power station in Israel is approximately twelve years.
limitations: These figures are reported through a Knesset hearing summary and should be attributed to the hearing and the presenting authority until the underlying Electricity Authority material is obtained.

A later July 2026 Knesset summary reports approximately 20,000 MW of connection requests. The difference may reflect rapid growth, scope or definition changes, and must be reconciled before a single current value is used.
MVA and MW are not interchangeable without assumptions about power factor.
audits.required_dataset_action: Represent grid connection as a constrained and uncertain capability. Preserve the 2025 figures as dated hearing-reported metrics, and create a research warning rather than replacing them with the unreconciled July 2026 figure.

audits.title: National AI Directorate presentation of the strategic program
exact_supported_claims: The National AI Directorate presented a national goal of access to 100,000 AI processors through private-sector construction with the state acting as a customer.
The presentation included promotion of AI data-center legislation, an ambition for an advanced chip plant, a national quantum computer and AI literacy and human-capital programs.
The committee discussion described infrastructure and human capital as top implementation priorities.
limitations: This is an official Knesset summary of a presentation, not the full text of Government Decision 4255.
The 100,000-processor goal is a policy target, not deployed capacity or a funded procurement commitment.
Detailed claims about five-year access, specific laboratories, sovereign spectrum and government data still require the official decision text.
audits.required_dataset_action: Upgrade Decision 4255 from unsupported to officially corroborated policy direction, while keeping the full decision source status pending and all target metrics non-operational.

audits.title: About AI21
exact_supported_claims: AI21 identifies its founders and current leadership and describes itself as a developer of enterprise AI systems and foundation models.
The page lists Israeli and international founders, advisers and investors.
limitations: The company page does not disclose a complete capitalization table, voting rights or verified country of ultimate control.
Headquarters, founder nationality or Israeli origin must not be treated as proof of domestic control.
audits.required_dataset_action: Keep AI21 as an Israel-origin and Israel-based model capability, but leave verified_control_country null and ownership_verification_status unverified_private_company.

audits.title: User-supplied INSS publication on chips and Israel
not_sufficient_for: Current production technology without primary corroboration
audits.required_dataset_action: Retain in contextual bibliography. Tower operational facts must use the 2026 SEC filing.

research_findings.finding: Israel has genuine domestic specialty-semiconductor fabrication through Tower Fab 2 and Intel Israel, but this does not close the leading-edge AI accelerator, HBM, EUV or advanced-packaging sovereignty gap.
The binding constraint for large Israeli AI data centers is not only planning permission. Grid connection, generation timing, location and demand concentration are material system constraints.
Government Decision 4255 is now officially corroborated at the strategic-direction level, but its full legal text remains missing from the research archive.
No defensible current national metric was found for water availability, cooling-water demand, backup generation or fuel-continuity requirements for Israeli AI data centers.

open_items: Obtain the underlying Electricity Authority or Noga presentation used in the November 2025 and July 2026 Knesset discussions.
Reconcile 2,500 MVA of requested connections reported in November 2025 with approximately 20,000 MW reported in July 2026.
Recover the full official text or official archive copy of Government Decision 4255.
Manually capture the title, date and claims of the exact INSS chips-israel page.
Research site-level water, cooling, backup generation and fuel-continuity requirements from planning or environmental documents.
Audit the legal status of Amendment 168 after final Knesset passage and publication.
